data.title: Design GPU Inference Serving System
data.contentPreview:
## 1. What is a GPU inference serving system?

A GPU inference serving system sits between users who send natural-language prompts and the GPU-accelerated models that generate responses. Its job is to accept many concurrent HTTP requests, efficiently group them into batches, dispatch those batches to a pool of GPU workers, and return individual responses quickly. The core challenge is squeezing maximum throughput from expensive, limited GPUs while keeping each user's wait time short.

## 2. Requirements

The core product tension is that users expect sub-second, individual completions, while GPUs are cost-effective only when processing large groups of inputs at once. A slow warm-up time for new GPU hardware makes dynamic allocation difficult under sudden traffic spikes.

### Clarifying Questions

::::qa-item
:::you[You]
"Does the inference response need to stream tokens progressively to the client as they are generated, or is a single synchronous completion returned when inference finishes?"
:::
:::interviewer[Interviewer]
"Single synchronous completion. The client sends a prompt and waits for the full response. No token streaming."
:::
:::takeaway[Takeaway]
Synchronous completion means the request path stays open for the full wait and execution time. Queueing delay therefore matters directly to the user-facing latency budget.
:::
::::

::::qa-item
:::you[You]
"What end-to-end latency is acceptable for a single inference request, and how much of that budget does the inference call itself consume?"
:::
:::interviewer[Interviewer]
"P99 under `500 ms` total. The inference execution itself takes about 100 milliseconds; the remaining `400 ms` is your total budget for network transfer and coordination."
:::
:::takeaway[Takeaway]
The non-inference overhead budget is tight. Batching helps cost efficiency, but it cannot be allowed to consume most of the user's latency budget.
:::
::::

::::qa-item
:::you[You]
"What are the constraints on how many requests can be grouped into a single inference call, and how fast can one GPU execute a batch?"
:::
:::interviewer[Interviewer]
"The inference function accepts between 1 and 100 inputs per call. One batch per GPU at a time, and each batch takes about 100 milliseconds."
:::
:::takeaway[Takeaway]
These constraints make batch size the main throughput and cost lever. The design has to keep GPUs reasonably full without violating latency targets.
:::
::::
